**Costs as returned.** On W-3902 the cost cells read "₦8,400,000.00", "₦14,000,000.00" and "₦3,150,000.00" at 1440 and at 390, with no short form. If the fixture's `"14000000.00"` is changed to `"14000000.10"`, the page shows "₦14,000,000.10" exactly. — verify: component test at both widths.
**The page computes nothing.**
**Unknown is never 0, blank or a dash.** W-3910 shows "Unknown" in the Toyota Hilux COST cell. That cell is not "₦0", "0.00", empty, "-" or "—". — verify: component test on W-3910.

**Sample-marked.** Every fixture page shows the shared `SampleLabel` ("SAMPLE DATA") because the record says `sample: true`. A copy with `sample: false` does not show it. — verify: component test; `jq '.sample' frontend/mock/fixtures/work/W-39*.json` all `true`.
**Each unset key is a hold with no controls.**
**Decide controls only from `you_can_act` and the steps.**
**Agent work is not a decision.**
**Approved and calculating only when the response says so.**

**Approve.** On W-3902 the page sends one E-TASK-CLAIM to `/api/v1/tasks/T-3902/claim`. Pressing "Approve register" then sends exactly one POST `/api/v1/tasks/T-3902/decision` with the CSRF header and `{verdict: "approve", expected_revision: 1}`. The body validates against the generated request schema, with no note and no extra keys. A double press sends one. The same holds for W-3903 and T-3903. — verify: component test; e2e request log.
**Return and reject need a note.**

**No write when the person cannot act.** On W-3901, W-3904, W-3905, W-3906, W-3907, W-3908, W-3909 and W-3912, no claim and no decision is sent, whatever is pressed or typed. — verify: e2e request log (zero task POSTs).

**Uncertain decide.** A network failure, timeout or 500 on decide re-reads the item before anything else and shows `UncertainNotice`. It never shows "approved", "returned" or "rejected" from the click, and sends no second decision automatically. A later deliberate decide clears the earlier notice. — verify: component test with fake timers (one POST after 60 s); e2e with a routed abort.

risk.rationale: High. This is a Finance approval of the register and dates that the asset schedule is built on, and the register-change rows carry money (₦14,000,000.00 disposal). A wrong control would make a Finance source look approved without the human decision. The rules at stake are the ones the product guards most closely: Unknown shown as 0, a browser-computed figure, an invented reviewer or rule, and an agent claim read as approval. The work stays contained: two decide tasks on the F-17 frame through F-33's inline Decide, on the mock, with nothing calculated or posted. The SURFACES are these: - ui: 8 boards. - api: E-WORK-ITEM and E-TASK-CLAIM/DECIDE. - security: an authority-bearing approval write. - contract-change: `fixed_assets` line, `steps[].verdict`, two tasks per item. - product-decision: all asset rules and F07 unset, plus D-RETURN open. PRODUCT-ACCEPTANCE is required, because this is a new Finance flow, it involves money, and the client has not seen it working.

findings.summary: The approve consequence ("3 assets have unclear dates; they go to a date review next.") sits below all three buttons, so it reads as if it applied to Return and Reject as well. Return and Reject state no consequence at all. Expected: each button is clear about what it does. Needs a decision on where the consequence is drawn, and wording for return and reject from the backend or the design engineer (D-RETURN is open); the frontend must not invent it.

The visually hidden "lifecycle" strip (DRAFTED, REVIEWED, APPROVED, SENT, RECEIPT RECORDED "Unknown", VERIFIED) is read by screen readers on every state. It disagrees with the screen: "Receipt recorded: Unknown" on a fixed asset schedule, "Reviewed: In progress" on the date review after the register is done, "Drafted: Not yet" on PROCESSING. It comes from the generic `facts` array on the base item. Fix the fixtures or drop the strip on this line so screen-reader users hear the same story as the stations.

The uncertain decide shows two stacked amber notices ("October register: result not confirmed" and "We are checking what happened. Nothing was sent again.") with the Reload button jammed against the sentence on desktop and wrapped awkwardly at 390. It reads correctly (never success) but should be one notice with spaced actions.

Conflicts 12 (D-118) approves only dropping the paperclip and the bold. It does not cover the capitals, the monospace grey or the move. A file name's case is part of the value. Expected: on the fixed_assets line, the cite label in its returned case, in body text (no capitals or mono), placed above "Uploaded · 64 KB", the way the board draws it. Scope it like the existing `.ws[data-line="fixed_assets"]` rules in `frontend/src/features/workspace/workspace.css:272-279` so F-33 and other lines are untouched. Then rewrite the "asset-dates-explanation.pdf" and "Uploaded · 64 KB" exceptions in `fidelity-exceptions.json` (keep them only if the tool still misses them once the text matches), and re-score the two date-review boards.

findings.summary: Investigating (W-3901, 1440 and 390): the register's values note "Chidi never reads asset values; he checks structure, dates and provenance." is drawn as the shared amber warning box with a warning icon. The board draws a plain muted line. This comes from Sections' facts `note`, which the approved spec chose (spec Decisions, "Values note"). The waiver covers it, but a warning tone on a reassurance is a change in meaning the design engineer should look at when signing the waiver.

Calculating (W-3904, 1440 and 390): the Calculate station is amber with "Waiting" (shared StationTrack). The board draws it blue for "in progress". The builder's reason holds: `current_agent` would draw "Agent working" for a factory step. It needs a station status for a running factory step from the backend (backend handoff). Waivable under D-83 until then. No Conflicts item covers it, so the design engineer signs it explicitly.

The frame's "History" link is under the project's 44px phone rule. Expected: at least 44 by 44 px (D-92c). Actual: 42×24 at 390 on every F-42 page and on F-33's W-2702. It still passes WCAG 2.2 AA target size (24px). It is shared F-17 frame code (`frontend/src/features/work-item/work-item.css:406`, `WorkItemView.tsx:151`), outside this feature's lane, and the builder's e2e excludes it explicitly (`e2e/asset-schedule.spec.ts:220`). It needs a frame-wide fix.

On the proof row, the file name is moved first with CSS `order: -1` (`frontend/src/features/workspace/workspace.css:282`), so the DOM order is "Uploaded · 64 KB" and then "asset-dates-explanation.pdf". A screen reader reads the detail before the file name. Expected: the reading order matches the visual order, with the file name first in the DOM.

Once, in run1 at 390, a forced 404 read showed "ERROR · COULDN'T LOAD … Reference unexpected_response" instead of the NO ACCESS view. That was at load average about 300. It did not recur in 4 later tries at 390 or in any try at 1440. No title, cost or asset leaked. I'm recording it as possible flakiness of the proxy or client under load, not as a defect.
